note: Holly/hulver is the standard English name for Ilex aquifolium; Culpeper gives no description.
Common St John's wort; pellucid-dotted opposite leaves, yellow star flowers.
Climbing on trees and church walls; the only native English ivy.
Common juniper bush; berries used medicinally.

headword: Kidneywort, Or Wall Pennyroyal, Or Wall Pennywort
note: Peltate saucer-like leaves on walls: wall pennywort/navelwort.
Common knapweed; scaly heads, purple florets; slightly torn leaves could also suggest greater knapweed.
Knotgrass is the standard name for Polygonum aviculare.
Round pleated lobed leaves: Alchemilla vulgaris aggregate.
Garden lavender of English gardens.
Lavender-cotton is the standard name of Santolina chamaecyparissus.
Meadow plant with pinnate leaves; lady's smock/cuckoo-flower.
Garden salad lettuce.
Covers white and yellow water lilies; main white kind Nymphaea alba, yellow Nuphar lutea.
Creeping root, white bell flowers, red berries.
White garden lily of 17th-century England is Lilium candidum.
Pinnate ash-like leaves; English-grown liquorice root.
Flat thallus on damp shady ground with small stalked star-like heads (receptacles) fits Marchantia.
Common yellow loosestrife, tall with leaves in pairs or whorls.

headword: Loosestrife, With Spiked Heads Of Flowers
note: Square stalks, long spikes of flowers; purple loosestrife.
Large winged leaves like smallage, hollow stalks; garden lovage.
Broad greyish leafy 'moss' on oaks and beeches without flowers: the lichen Lobaria pulmonaria.
Garden madder: rough square trailing stems, whorled leaves.
Black brittle stalks with small round leaflets: English 'common maidenhair' = Asplenium trichomanes.
Wall rue/white maidenhair is Asplenium ruta-muraria.
Hair-like leaves and golden capsule in a husk, in bogs/heaths: haircap moss.
Common mallow plus marshmallow (Althaea officinalis), both described.
No description; field maple is the native English maple.
Called Origanum, wild or field marjoram.
Garden sweet marjoram; pot marjoram mentioned (O. onites).
Garden marigold of English herbals is Calendula officinalis.
Common masterwort with ternate leaves; GBIF-accepted name, syn. Peucedanum ostruthium.
Yellow tansy-like flower heads, narrow toothed leaves: sweet maudlin.
Medlar tree described; five-petalled white flowers.
Yellow scented trefoil flowers: melilot/King's claver.
French mercury, annual and branched, is Mercurialis annua.
Dog mercury, unbranched stalks, woodland.
Spear or heart mint explicitly described.
Woody parasite with paired leaves on tree branches.
Creeping stems with paired round leaves: moneywort/herb twopence.
Single divided leaf with fertile spike: moonwort fern.
Unspecified ground moss (bryophytes) and tree moss (epiphytic mosses/lichens); no description given.
Square stalk, lobed leaves, whorled flowers: motherwort.
Stoloniferous hairy rosette, milky sap, single pale yellow head.
Leaves dark green above, white beneath; tall stalks.
Mulberry grown in 17th-century England was the black mulberry.
Common white mullein with woolly leaves, tall stalk.
Rough beaked pods with round yellowish seed fit white mustard; black mustard also possible.
Tough branched stalk, runcinate leaves: hedge mustard.
Tiny annual with small white flowers: whitlow grass.
Garden nep/catmint, hoary square stalks.
Stinging nettles; both common and small nettle covered.
Common nightshade with basil-like leaves and black berries.
English oak; no description.
Cultivated oats.
One/two ribbed leaves, white star flowers: one-blade.
Tuberous orchids collectively (dog-stones, satyrion); only roots described.
Garden onion.
Fleshy leaves, tufted flowers, tuberous roots: orpine.
Garden parsley.

headword: Parsley Piert, Or Parsley Break Stone
note: Small prostrate plant with parsley-like leaves: parsley piert.
Garden and wild parsnip; wild described.
Large rough pinnate leaves; cow parsnip is hogweed.
Peach tree described.
Pear trees.
Single flower white above, reddish beneath; English wild sort described is sneezewort.
Reddish brittle stems on walls; British species is P. judaica, older texts say P. officinalis.
Common pennyroyal, creeping mint.
Male peony (entire leaflets) = P. mascula; female = P. officinalis.
Broad bluish leaves, white flowers, tall: dittander.
Trailing rooting stems, small shiny leaves, pale blue flowers in woods.
Square stalks, larger and with few dots, damp places; Ascyron of herbals.
Square trailing stalks, sessile paired leaves, single flowers: scarlet pimpernel.
Low hairy plant with three-cleft leaves, pine scent: Chamaepitys.
Common plantain of paths and meadows.
Plums.
Winged fronds on oaks: polypody of the oak.
White and black poplar both described.
White and black garden poppies = P. somniferum; corn rose = P. rhoeas.
Garden purslane salad herb.
Primroses.
Common privet for arbours and topiary.

headword: Queen Of The Meadows, Meadow Sweet, Or Mead Sweet
note: Reddish stalks, elm-like pinnate leaves: meadowsweet.
Quince tree described.
Horse-radish described; garden radish (Raphanus sativus) only named.
St James-wort/staggerwort with torn leaves: common ragwort.
Yellow rattle (cock's-comb leaves) and red rattle (lousewort) both described.
Woody twigs armed with short sharp thorns: restharrow (GBIF includes O. repens as subsp. procurrens).
Wild rocket with finely cut leaves, yellow flowers, long pods; garden rocket omitted.
Winter-rocket/winter cresses with lyrate leaves.
Garden roses (red, white, damask) and briar roses collectively.
Round leaves with red glandular hairs, moist in heat: sundew.
Garden rosemary.
Garden-grown rhubarb in England with huge round sour leaves: rhapontic.
Garden patience/monk's rhubarb is Rumex patientia.

headword: Great Round-Leaved Dock, Or Bastard Rhubarb
note: Large round leaves, yellow root resembling rhubarb: alpine dock.
Yellow stringy creeping root, divided leaves: meadow rue.
Garden rue, herb of grace.
Prostrate thready branches, tiny yellowish flowers: rupturewort.
Bulrushes and soft rushes collectively; no description.
Rye grain.
Saffron.
Garden sage.
Wood-sage with hoary square stalks, sage-like leaves.
Arching stalk with alternate leaves like lily of the valley.
Rock samphire explicitly described.
Palmately lobed glossy leaves: wood sanicle.
Man-high, willow-like toothed leaves, yellow star flowers: Solidago saracenica of herbals.
Jack-by-the-hedge with nettle-shaped leaves, white flowers.
Summer (S. hortensis) and winter (S. montana) savory.
Savine, evergreen garden shrub.
Small reddish bulbils (kernels) at the root: white meadow saxifrage.
Burnet saxifrage with white umbels; greater sort is P. major.
Common field scabious with pale blue heads; smaller sort likely S. columbaria.
English scurvygrass with long-stalked fleshy leaves.
Self-heal, prunel, carpenter's herb.
No description; fruit eaten mellow like medlars; native English service tree (syn. Sorbus torminalis).
Shepherd's purse.
Smallage is wild celery.
Creeping jointed roots, plantain-like ribbed leaves: soapwort.
Ordinary sorrel of gardens and fields.
Trefoil leaves notched at the ends: wood sorrel.
Sow thistles.
Southernwood.
Hair-fine leaves, aromatic root: spignel/baldmoney.
Fronds lobed to midrib, rusty scales beneath, on walls: Ceterach.
Star thistle with spreading branches.
Strawberries.
Garden and wild succory with blue flowers.
Trailing stonecrop on walls and roofs; cooling, harmless virtues suggest S. album, not hot wall-pepper.
English tobacco, smaller than the Indian kind.
No description; tamarisk of western Europe.
Garden tansy.
Wild tansy/silverweed.
Many English thistles treated collectively without description.
Hoary stalk, weakly prickly leaves, single head.
White-veined prickly leaves: our lady's thistle.
Woolly prickly leaves, crimson florets; duplicates Down or Cotton Thistle entry.
Clothworkers' teasel with hooked bracts; wild teasel also described.
Round notched pouches, entire leaves, white flowers, garlic smell.
Taller biennial, smaller round pouches, sharper taste; names applied to both species.
Blackthorn/sloe.
Perfoliate bluish leaves: thorough-wax.
Garden thyme.

headword: Wild Thyme, Or Mother Of Thyme
note: Wild/mother of thyme; British plants mostly T. praecox, historically T. serpyllum.
Like cinquefoil but with stalkless leaves: tormentil/septfoil.
Greater turnsole: hoary annual, white flowers on curled spike, Mediterranean.
Meadow trefoil; red and white honeysuckles.
Leaf with heart-shaped flesh-coloured spot fits spotted medick.
Common trefoil with white pearl-like leaf spot; no further description.
Tutsan, park leaves.
Garden valerian with entire then pinnate leaves, thick root above ground.
Common vervain with square branched stalks.
Vine.
Tame and wild violets.
Rough prickly stalks; viper's bugloss.
Single yellow wild wallflowers on walls.
Walnut tree.
Dyer's weed, rosette of narrow leaves.
All kinds of wheat; main one bread wheat.
Willows collectively; no description.
Woad, bluish plantain-like leaves.
Woodbine/honeysuckle.
Common wormwood main; sea wormwood and Roman wormwood also treated.

headword: Yarrow, Called Nose-Bleed, Milfoil And Thousand-Leal
note: Yarrow/milfoil.
